SLR BUI 1 Tier 3 Analysis

Aaron Dain

Tier 3 Analysis for mercury in Walleye for the St. Lawrence River (Cornwall/Akwesasne) AOC

Reference Sites


The following reference sites were used in the Tier 3 analysis of mercury in Walleye for the AOC:


AOC

  • St. Lawrence River 15 - Cornwall Island South
  • St. Lawrence River 15 - Cornwall Waterfront
  • St. Lawrence River 15 - Lake St. Francis

Reference

  • Lake Ontario 10 - Middle Bay of Quinte
  • Lake Ontario 11 - Lower Bay of Quinte/Eastern Lake Ontario
  • Lake Ontario 2 - Twelve Mile Creek Port Dalhousie
  • Lake Ontario 4a - Toronto Waterfront
  • Lake Ontario 6 - Northwestern
  • Lake Ontario 8
  • Lake Ontario 9 - Upper Bay of Quinte
  • Lake Ontario 9a - Trenton Nearshore
  • Lake Ontario 9b - Belleville Nearshore
  • St. Lawrence River 12 - Lower Thousand Island
  • St. Lawrence River 13
  • St. Lawrence River 15 - Cornwall - St Regis Island S


Tier 3A: Virtual Advisory for mercury in Walleye

Virtual advisory values were generated using by modelling the relationship between fish length and contaminant concentration for Walleye and mercury. For each region, the function fits a log-log linear model (lm(log(Value) ~ log(Length)) to evaluate whether a significant relationship exists (p ≤ 0.05). If so, predicted concentrations are generated across a continuous length range, and then averaged within fixed 5 cm bins. Advisory levels are assigned using MECP-defined contaminant- and population-specific (General/Sensitive) thresholds to the mean predicted concentrations. If no significant relationship is detected, advisory levels are based on the mean concentration of all observations within each bin.

(ref:Virtual-advisory-visualization) Virtual mercury advisories in Walleye. Predicted concentrations (curve) and observed values (points) by region using power regression model, compared to MECP advisory limits for MERCURY (dashed lines).



Model Summary by Region: {-}

AOC: There is a statistically significant relationship between fish length and contaminant concentration. The power model used was: concentration = 0.000188 × Length2.001 (R² = 0.806, p = < 0.001). Reference: There is a statistically significant relationship between fish length and contaminant concentration. The power model used was: concentration = 2.26e-05 × Length2.393 (R² = 0.712, p = < 0.001).

(#tab:virtual-advisory-table) Virtual advisory levels for mercury in Walleye across regions. Values represent meals/month recommendations. Red cells indicate restrictive virtual advisory falling below the desired consumption rate of 8 meals/month; green cells indicate unrestrictive virtual advisory equal to or above the desired consumption rate.

General population: Of 13 size bins, 5 were below the desired consumption rate of 8 meals/month. Of these, 4 were more restrictive than reference. Sensitive population: Of 13 size bins, 9 were below the desired consumption rate of 8 meals/month. Of these, 6 were more restrictive than reference.


Tier 3A Overall Decision: Unsupportive


Tier 3B: Comparison of contaminant concentrations in Walleye in AOC to reference

To assess differences in fish contamination between the AOC and reference sites, contaminant–length relationships were modeled using Generalized Additive Models (GAMs), allowing for non-linear associations. For each priority contaminant and indicator species, we first tested whether the shape of the concentration–length relationship differed significantly between AOC and reference fish. Where models supported statistically similar trends (non-significant interaction), we compared size-adjusted contaminant levels using estimated marginal means. Where shapes differed significantly, contaminant concentration values were compared by GAM-predicted values at standardized lengths (e.g., 45cm) commonly consumed for each fish species. A threshold of α = 0.05 was used to evaluate statistical significance throughout.

(ref:Tier-3B-Figure) mercury concentration in Walleye by length in the AOC compared to reference sites. Points are observed contaminant values, curves represent GAM model fit (with random effects dropped for simplicity, fitted across the 1st to 99th percentile of data to ensure reasonable support), ribbons represent 95% confidence interval.

(#tab:tier-3b-summary-table) Predicted mercury concentrations (µg/g) in Walleye, estimated using generalized additive models (GAMs) across the observed range of fish lengths where data is available for both groups. Values represent model-predicted means with 95% confidence intervals. Asterisks (*) indicate size classes where the AOC differs significantly (p < 0.05) from reference.


Generalized Additive Models (GAMs) were used to model the relationship between fish length and mercury concentrations for walleye in the AOC and reference regions. The length-contaminant relationship did not differ significantly between sites (interaction test p = 0.0916). Marginal mean concentrations were estimated across the full size distribution using a reduced model with shared smooths. The estimated marginal mean Mercury concentration in the AOC was -0.94 µg/g (95% CI: -1.24–-0.64). Estimated values for reference site(s): Reference: -1.51 µg/g (95% CI: -1.67–-1.34).

The AOC has a higher marginal mean concentration than reference, suggesting elevated contamination in this species compared to reference.


Tier 3B Overall Decision: Unsupportive


Tier 3C: Temporal Trends

Temporal trends in Walleye for mercury were assessed using linear models across all years of data. An initial model tested for a significant interaction between fish length and sampling year. If an interaction was detected, trends were evaluated separately for the three most frequently sampled length bins. Otherwise, annual mean contaminant concentrations were used. Trends help support Tier 3C by assessing if contaminant levels have declined, remained stable, or increased over time. A half-life for mercury concentrations in Walleye was predicted for the AOC and reference sites using a generalized additive mixed model (GAMM). The log values of mercury concentration were estimated using year as a linear predictor by region, with smooth effects controlling for fish length. Sampling sites were used as random effects to account for repeated sampling. The slope (on log scale) represents the annual rate of change in mercury concentration, defined as k = -slope.

Time to reach an unrestrictive advisory of 8 meals/month for upper-quartile-length fish
Upper Quantile Length (cm) Predicted Conc. (Current Year) Unrestrictive Conc. Years to Threshold 95% CI Outcome
60 0.60 0.16 86.8 67.9–105.7 Unsupportive

A model test was performed to estimate the time required to reach a nonrestrictive monthly meal allowance for the upper quantile fish length (rounded to the nearest 5 cm) for sensitive populations. A timeline of 10 years or fewer is considered supportive of delisting, whereas a timeline of 10 or more years is unsupportive.

For upper-quartile length (60 cm) fish, it is predicted to take about 86.8 years (95% CI 67.9–105.7) to reach an unrestrictive monthly meal allowance of 8 meals/month for the Sensitive population. Therefore, Tier 3C is considered .
